A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReflectDiffu and contain readable main text and Appendices A–D. Their methods, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary analyses can be matched despite reflow and limited additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original automatic evaluations, component ablations, and human A/B results in Tables 2–3, plus emotion–intent frequency analysis and case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional baseline scores and case-study responses in Tables 2, 4, and 5.

M1.justification: The emotion-reason annotator, contagion encoder, contrastive experts, Intent Twice RL-diffusion procedure, decoder, and losses remain unchanged. Explicitly calling the existing loss coefficients hyperparameters does not introduce a new objective or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use EMPATHETICDIALOGUES with emotion-reason and intent annotations, plus EMPATHETICINTENT for classifier training. The dialogue tasks and case-study contexts remain the same; no new dataset, domain, or test population is evaluated.

E2.justification: V3 adds IAMM and Harnessing (0-shot) to automatic evaluation and both case studies (Tables 2, 4–5). Table 3 retains the same human comparators. The removed ChatGLM-6B mention in Appendix B.2 of v1 had no corresponding result row.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces zero-shot GPT-4o evaluation with a stated 30-token budget for the added Harnessing baseline. Existing data splits, ReflectDiffu training settings, metrics, and human evaluation procedures remain unchanged; v3 explicitly excludes the two new baselines from human evaluation.

E4.justification: The two case studies gain IAMM and Harnessing responses, and Table 5 replaces the Qwen and Llama responses with ones relevant to the graduate-school context. The four component ablations and Appendix B.1 emotion–intent frequency analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The three-annotator evaluation and descriptive frequency analysis retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds IAMM and Harnessing scores while retaining all existing numerical entries; Table 3 is unchanged. Harnessing now leads Distinct-1/2 at 1.79/14.72, versus ReflectDiffu's unchanged 0.98/4.35. Tables 4–5 also add or replace qualitative response entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(20), including Appendix C's annotator and classification losses, retain their substance. Changes to function typography and punctuation do not alter mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The introduction drops construction and release of the annotated multi-task dataset as a separately stated contribution, although Section 4.1 retains the annotation work. The central framework, emotion–intent alignment, and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds interpretations of the IAMM and Harnessing comparisons, including a claim of zero-shot robustness. The PDFs report zero-shot settings for Harnessing, without a corresponding zero-shot evaluation of ReflectDiffu. The existing computational limitations and mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 removes the dataset-availability statement and anonymous resource link without providing a replacement access route. Appendix A.1 adds GPT-4o and token-budget information for Harnessing; existing annotation-model links, hardware, optimizer, and training details remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations and descriptions for IAMM and Harnessing, plus citations to Cultural Palette and diffusion-based Bayesian optimization. These are limited additions; the broader positioning around psychological mechanisms and RL-guided diffusion is retained.

P1.justification: Edits include author/contact information, CoT terminology, punctuation, the shortened contribution list, and localized additions to baseline descriptions and results discussion. The section and appendix sequence remains unchanged, with most prose retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains larger type, abbreviated headings, revised rules, and an explanatory caption. Tables 4–5 gain rows, while tables and the heatmap move with text reflow. All three figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3 broadens baseline comparisons, replaces context-inappropriate Table 5 responses, and improves Table 2 legibility. However, it removes the dataset-access statement and link and introduces a zero-shot robustness interpretation unsupported by a reported zero-shot evaluation of ReflectDiffu. These benefits and weaknesses leave the net effect on overall paper quality uncertain.
